name: browser_history
description: Query a browser history database from a copy of it and its -wal, -shm and -journal sidecars, made under the job's $OUT or the agent's own directory and removed afterwards. Named queries: chrome_visits and firefox_visits (every visit joined to its URL: visit id, raw time and microsecond ISO time, transition or visit type with its raw value, referring visit), chrome_url_summary and firefox_url_summary (ONE ROW PER URL with a visit count and the last visit: a summary, not a visit list; chrome_history and firefox_history are their old names, answered with a note), chrome_downloads, firefox_downloads, tables; or your own SELECT, WITH or PRAGMA. Read-only twice: a statement must start with SELECT, WITH or PRAGMA, and the copy is opened with a SQLite authorizer that denies every action but reading and the pragmas that only report. It reports wal_present (a -wal was beside the database) and wal_frames_replayed (valid frames SQLite found in it and checkpointed into the copy; 0 for a damaged log), never merely that a sidecar was copied. SENSITIVE: before any query, every text or BLOB cell of a credential column (logins.password_value, cookies.value and encrypted_value, moz_cookies.value, Firefox key4.db metadata and nssPrivate, and any column whose name says password, secret, token, encrypted or card number) is replaced in the copy by a marker holding only its length, and the answer lists what was withheld; no flag brings a value back, and nothing is decrypted. Usernames, URLs and dates are returned. A BLOB column is returned whole as hex; select what you need.

path.description: Path to History, places.sqlite or another SQLite database

query.description: chrome_visits | chrome_url_summary | chrome_downloads | firefox_visits | firefox_url_summary | firefox_downloads | tables (chrome_history and firefox_history still answer, as the URL summaries)

sql.description: Your own SELECT, WITH or PRAGMA, instead of a named query

limit.description: Rows shown inline per statement (default 200, at most 20000, an inline page size); every row is kept, and when there are more the whole list is written as JSON Lines and named in all_results
